terms.gloss: to name a day for someone’s trial, to summon or impeach him
evidence: Cic. Mil. 36: diem mihi, crēdō, dīxerat (Lewis & Short s.v. diēs)

terms.gloss: to serve a summons on someone
terms.comment: Traupman’s phrase. We have found no classical instance of diem dare in this sense; the classical phrase is diem dīcere.

evidence: Ter. Ph. 936: in jūs ambulā (see court)

sources: Lewis & Short: dies · Lewis & Short: voco
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 196, each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
